text:
skye: Heads up, small but nasty: types in our ESM bundle are sometimes collapsing generic overloads -> gets consumers `any`. Seen when packaged with rollup-plugin-dts. Anyone got tips?

jordan: I have. Usually the problem is post-processing of .d.ts files. Are we using tsc -> rollup-plugin-dts or rollup to generate d.ts directly?

skye: tsc emits .d.ts, then we run a plugin that concatenates and rewrites. Locally tsc output looks correct, packaged dts has fallen back to non-generic signature.

maya: Can you share a micro repro? Overloads + generic erasure are common failure modes.

skye: Tiny repro:
```ts
// lib.ts
export function call<T>(p: string): Promise<T>;
export async function call(p: string) { return fetch(p).then(r => r.json()) }
// consumer.ts
const a = await call<{x:number}>("/x");
// in some packaged builds a is any
```

jordan: If the bundled d.ts loses the generic it's the bundler. Quick fixes: 1) export a single generic signature instead of overloads 2) make tsc output canonical and copy it into dist without transforming 3) use declarationMap to trace origins.

frank: Also check package.json `types`/`exports` mapping. Some consumers resolve types via `exports.types` or `types` field and can pick the wrong file. ESM entries can point to a different .d.ts.

maya: Another subtle thing: default export vs named changes how TS infers for mixed CJS consumers. Prefer named exports for the SDK.

jordan: Long term we should add a CI test: npm pack the artifact, install it into a tiny test app, run `tsc --noEmit` to ensure declarations work for both NodeNext and classic consumers.

skye: For now I switched to single generic signature `export function call<T = unknown>(p: string): Promise<T>` and updated package types to point to tsc output. That fixed the consumer errors in ESM.

build-bot: [pack-check #88] failed earlier: "dts mismatch: packaged types missing generic overload" — logs: https://ci.redwood/pack-check/88

frank: I'll open a quick RFC to 1) stop transforming tsc .d.ts, 2) add packed-package tsc smoke test, 3) lint rule to discourage ambiguous overloads that only differ by return generic.

maya: +1. Also add a CONTRIBUTING note about export shape parity and prefer named exports.

jordan: If anyone needs a helper script I wrote a tiny `verify-dts.sh` that runs npm pack, extracts, and runs tsc in a sample project. Happy to PR it.

skye: Please PR it. Saved my afternoon. Leaving this thread so others know the ESM/CJS + d.ts combo can produce `any` surprises. :memo:
